conventions.convention: Independent cells have finite nonzero Hilbert-space dimension, commuting Hermitian Hamiltonian and number operator, and no intercell interaction. Geometric inputs retain whole-future-mass-shell stationarity, a global potential compensator, and Countable Choice.
The total partition sum is Z=product Zi; the selected-cell density uses Z_loc=Zi.
Physical time is measured in seconds, KMS strip width is βℏ, and α^λ_τ=α_(τ/λ) has inverse temperature λβ. Along the selected Killing orbit, τ=Nt_K with constant positive dimensionless lapse N.
Controls have sign G−εhB; the response kernel has sign +i/ℏ. Observables and controls commute with number. Killing-time control amplitude is Nh(Nt), while R_K(t)=R_loc(Nt).

The Fourier convention uses exp(iωt). Spectral measures are pushed forward by ω↦Nω, preserving atomic masses; the coth relation excludes zero frequency. Static susceptibility concerns a separately normalized Gibbs family.
Sequence indices start at zero; inner products are linear in the first argument. Completeness means convergence of every norm-Cauchy sequence.
The rotating generator is the closure of H−ΩJ on D(N). At a=ε−ℏmΩ=0 its closure is zero on the entire Hilbert space. The obstruction excludes only the specified normalized trace-Gibbs form.

load_bearing.statement: Under the stated finite independent-cell and charged stationary-geometry hypotheses, G_K=sum_i N_i(H_i−μ_iQ_i), Z=product_i Z_i, and ρ=tensor_i ρ_i. The state is β_K-KMS for grand-generator dynamics; its restriction to observables commuting with total number is β_K-KMS for physical H_K dynamics.

For a selected constructed finite cell and neutral Hermitian observables and controls, E_K(t)=E_loc(Nt) on 0≤t≤S/N, with identical rescaled first-order terms and quadratic remainder bounds. S_K=(D_N)_*S_loc. The separately re-prepared static susceptibility is β_loc Cov_KM,σ(B,B)≥0.

With the inner product and norm of def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set, the complex sequence space ℓ²(N₀,C) is complete. Hence it is a complex Hilbert space in the sense of def-hilbert-space.
For constant λ>0, a β_K-KMS state for α is λβ_K-KMS for α^λ_τ=α_(τ/λ); conversely, a β̂-KMS state for α^λ is (β̂/λ)-KMS for α. The selected metric-defined Killing orbit has τ=Nt_K and β_loc=Nβ_K.

The occupation partition sum sum_(n≥0) exp(−β_Kan) is finite exactly when a=ε−ℏmΩ>0, when it equals 1/(1−exp(−β_Ka)) and defines the displayed diagonal Gibbs state. For a≤0 no normalized Gibbs state of this trace form exists.

concerns.concern: Proof step 3.1 calls D(N) the 'dense finite-support domain'. D(N) contains infinite-support sequences, for example x_n=2^(−n). Step 1.1 correctly establishes density through its finite-support subset. The closure argument remains valid; the domain description should say 'dense domain'.
